contents.text:
I'm settling on the provider picture: the docs describe one IChatClient layer over Anthropic, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible backends, each kept in its own project behind ILlmProvider. I'll cite docs/GOAL.md and ADR 0092, write the answer in short paragraphs rather than a list, put code in backticks, and close by offering a few choices.

I'm settling on how to phrase the caveat about `CliHost.RunAsync` and its `args`: a prompt given on the command line gets a one-shot answer and then exits, otherwise it runs interactively. I'll point to the paths in the CLI project doc, ADR 0091, GOAL.md, and ADR 0076, then close by offering a few follow-up choices.

This program starts the coding agent in the terminal. It names what the agent may be and do, then hands that to a host that runs it.

The `using` lines bring in the framework's libraries. `LouisAgent.Core.Web` and `LouisAgent.Core.Telemetry` are the web and the tracer, and the three provider namespaces are the model backends. `LouisAgent.Cli` is the terminal host and `LouisAgent.Coding` is this demo's catalogue. The comment says the command takes an optional prompt.

`CliHost.RunAsync(args, ...)` is the one call the program makes. Its first argument is the command line. With a prompt, it answers once and exits. Without one, it opens the interactive chat. It builds the engine with `AgentHost.Build`, then runs a `ConsoleChat` over it. [`src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md`](https://github.com/bosbevk/louis-agent/blob/main/src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md) covers this in its Starting section.

`CodingCatalog.Create()` is the catalogue. It is the list of identities and packs this program loads. The page says the coding agent's catalogue names three identities, with `CodingIdentity` first, and nine packs. The host does not pick packs itself. The program names them, because a library cannot reference another project's packs. That is the rule in [`src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md`](https://github.com/bosbevk/louis-agent/blob/main/src/docs/projects/LouisAgent.Cli.md).

`new HostServices(...)` lends the host the parts it needs but does not own. `WebAccess.Create` gives the agent web access. `OtlpTelemetry.Instance` sends traces to an OpenTelemetry collector. Each part has a null version, so a program that omits one still runs. The `Providers:` list gives the model backends: Anthropic, Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible server. Each provider sits behind one seam, so the engine does not care which one answers. [`src/docs/adr/0091-web-access-and-telemetry-are-libraries-on-core.md`](https://github.com/bosbevk/louis-agent/blob/main/src/docs/adr/0091-web-access-and-telemetry-are-libraries-on-core.md) covers the web and telemetry parts. [`src/docs/GOAL.md`](https://github.com/bosbevk/louis-agent/blob/main/src/docs/GOAL.md) covers the providers.

The idea to keep: core ships no agent. The identities and packs come from the catalogue the program names, so changing the agent means changing that list. [`src/docs/adr/0076-core-ships-no-agent.md`](https://github.com/bosbevk/louis-agent/blob/main/src/docs/adr/0076-core-ships-no-agent.md) gives the reason.
